blocks.x: As streaming platforms go, Hulu truly has something for everyone. Not only does it feature a ton of original programming in its own right, its sprawling library includes access to a slew of new and classic series from other networks (whether they have their own streaming apps or not). Through its FX partnership, Hulu is also home to the entire FX library, as well as FX on Hulu collaborations (like The Bear) that don’t air linearly.

For those looking for some spooky season-themed programming this October, Hulu is the home of the new season of American Horror Story, which features a bevy of returning big-name cast members like Jessica Lange, Sarah Paulson, Evan Peters, Angela Bassett, and Kathy Bates for a 13th outing that mixes characters from across many of its various iterations into a single story. Other notable horror-themed recent additions include German drama City Of Blood, a dystopian vampire series set in a heat-ravaged Berlin.
Here are more of our picks for the best shows streaming on Hulu right now.
This list was updated on October 6, 2026.
Stars: Malik Elassal, Lucy Freyer, Jack Innanen, Amita Rao, and Owen Thiele

Every generation gets a hangout comedy, and FX’s Adults is Gen Z’s answer to shows like Friends and New Girl. The story of five twentysomethings living together in Queens will feel familiar to almost anyone, but the series updates familiar tropes with timely subplots about social media, economic struggles, and relationship drama. The ensemble cast’s warm found family vibe is what makes even the most ridiculous subplots work.
Stars: Matthew Rhys, Keri Russell, Noah Emmerich, Alison Wright, Holly Taylor, Margo Martindale, Annet Mahendru, Keidrich Sellati, Costa Ronin

FX’s award-winning The Americans will rightfully go down in history as one of television’s finest. Created by Joe Weisberg and Joel Fields, the ’80s-set drama works effectively as a riveting Cold War thriller about two Russian agents who settle down in Washington, D.C., and start a family. It’s an even better meditation on marriage and love as it dissects the relationship between Philip and Elizabeth Jennings. (And with co-stars Rhys and Russell having a moment with Widow’s Bay and The Diplomat respectively, there’s rarely been a better time for a rewatch.)
Stars: Donald Glover, Brian Tyree Henry, Zazie Beetz, LaKeith Stanfield, Isiah Whitlock Jr.

In a post-Community world, Glover found more mainstream success as musician Childish Gambino and through his FX comedy, Atlanta. This isn’t to say the show is by any means mainstream. In it, he plays Earn Marks, a rookie manager trying to get his cousin Paper Boi’s (Henry) rap career to take off. Over four seasons, Atlanta evolved into a sharp, incisive series with nuanced observations on race and societal issues.
Stars: Jeremy Allen White, Ayo Edebiri, Ebon Moss-Bachrach, Liza Colón-Zayas, Lionel Boyce, Abby Elliott

Created by Christopher Storer, the big-hearted dramedy sees chef Carmen “Carmy” Berzatto (White) running his family’s Italian beef sandwich shop in Chicago after the death of his brother—and then turning that spot into a fine-dining destination. The series concluded with its fifth and final season in June 2026
Stars: Amanda Seyfried, Naveen Andrews, William H. Macy, Dylan Minnette, Bill Irwin, Laurie Metcalf, Sam Waterston, Camryn Mi-Young Kim, Stephen Fry, Kate Burton, Elizabeth Marvel, Mary Lynn Rajskub

Come to The Dropout for Amanda Seyfried’s award-winning, chilling turn as Theranos’ Elizabeth Holmes; stay for Naveen Andrews’ even more deranged take on her partner, Sunny Balwani. The two ran their company to the ground while scamming folks into giving them money for an advanced blood-testing machine that didn’t exist. Hulu’s limited series is an enticing depiction of the events, digging into how Elizabeth and Sunny manage to get investors while running a tight, paranoid ship at the office.
Stars: Máiréad Tyers, Bilal Hasna, Sofia Oxenham, Luke Rollason, Siobhán McSweeney,

A superhero series for those who are tired of superhero series, this canceled-too-soon dramedy is set in a world where everyone gains a superpower at 18. Except for Jen Regan (Tyers), an underachieving twentysomething who has yet to manifest any sort of special ability at all. As Jen struggles to figure out what it means to lack powers in a world defined by them, she and her (oddly superpowered) friends face the frequently hilarious and heartbreaking trials of young adulthood, from relationship issues to career stagnation.
Stars: Emmy Rossum, Lola Petticrew, Quincy Tyler Bernstine, Scoot McNairy, Jake Lacy, Steve Way, Hope Davis, and Rob Yang.

A smart, subversive take on the crime procedural, this series technically follows a cat-and-mouse chase between an FBI agent (Rossum) and a female serial killer (Petticrew). But the characters are much more complicated than they initially appear, and the show deftly intertwines their complex histories of trauma and abuse to create a compelling exploration of institutional failure, rage, and survival. The series has been renewed for a second season.
Stars: Elle Fanning, Nicholas Hoult, Sacha Dhawan, Phoebe Fox, Gwilym Lee, Charity Wakefield, Adam Godley, Belinda Bromilow

Tony McNamara’s historical comedy isn’t really a true story at all. It is loosely—like, extremely loosely—based on the life of Russian Empress Catherine The Great (Fanning), who usurps power from her cruel husband, Peter III (Hoult). The show has one hell of a time depicting how she plots to overtake his kingdom—all while avoiding falling in love with him.
Cast: Elisabeth Moss, Joseph Fiennes, Yvonne Strahovski, Alexis Bledel, Madeline Brewer, Ann Dowd, O-T Fagbenle, Max Mingella, Samira Wiley, Amanda Brugel, Bradley Whitford

The Emmy-winning adaptation of Margaret Atwood’s classic novel of the same name, The Handmaid’s Tale arrived at the timeliest possible political moment in the spring of 2017, and kept right on being uncomfortably prescient all the way through its series finale eight years later. Set in Gilead, a totalitarian theocracy where fertility rates have plummeted and the women still capable of conceiving are basically kept as slaves, the series centers on June (Moss), a handmaid struggling to survive and, later, to resist the horrific world she is trapped in.
Stars: Daisy Edgar-Jones, Paul Mescal, Sarah Greene, Aislin McGuckin, Sebastian De Souza

Few adaptations feel as innately “correct” as Normal People, Hulu’s hugely affectionate adaptation of Sally Rooney’s beloved romance novel. Across 12 half-hour episodes, each more tender than the last, Marianne (Edgar-Jones) and Connell (Mescal) come of age while falling in and out of love along Ireland’s coast. The result is a tortured fantasy that will leave you agonizing for several hours in the most satisfying way imaginable.
Stars: Martin Short, Steve Martin, Selena Gomez, Da’Vine Joy Randolph, Michael Cyril-Creighton, Jackie Hoffman

Only Murders In The Building might just be Hulu’s most consistent offering to date. Short and Martin are frequent and terrific collaborators, but their pairing with Gomez made the series an immediate gem, with the three playing residents of a fancy New York City building who do a true-crime podcast. The star-studded fifth round wrapped up last fall, and the gang will head to London in season six.
Stars: Sterling K. Brown, James Marsden, Julianne Nicholson, Sarah Shahi, Krys Marshall, Nicole Brydon Bloom, Jon Beavers

Dan Fogelman brings This Is Us‘ sentimentality to the political thriller Paradise, which charts the investigation of a Secret Service agent (played by Brown) into the death of Marsden’s former POTUS. However, nothing is as simple as it looks—and this drama is chock-full of crazy twists that will suck you in. The series has been renewed for a third and final season.
Stars: Maya Erskine, Anna Konkle, Taj Cross, Mutsuko Erskine, Richard Karn, Melora Walters, Dallas Liu, Taylor Nichols

Cringe comedy is never easy to get through, and Pen15 has heaps of it. We’re talking full-body shudders. Created by Erskine and Konkle, the two play 13-year-old versions of themselves, as they try to survive eighth grade and all the issues that come with it: first crushes, AIM chats (remember those?), pool parties, and early stages of friendships. Pen15 is painfully awkward sometimes, but damn if it doesn’t remain endearing from start to finish.
Stars: MJ Rodriguez, Indya Moore, Billy Porter, Dominique Jackson, Hailie Sahar, Ryan Jamal Swain, Angel Bismark Curiel, Angelica Ross

There isn’t another show quite like Pose. Set in the 1980s, it dives into New York City’s ball-culture scene, assembling a history-making cast with multiple trans actors, led by Rodriguez. She plays Blanca, the mother of House of Evangelista, who takes in a number of struggling young folks. While it features the hardships that LGBTQ+ and people of color went through during the time, Pose is still effervescent and joyous as it celebrates their existence.
Stars: Ramy Youssef, Hiam Abbass, May Calamawy, Mohammed Amir, Amr Waked, Steve Way, Laith Nakli, Mahershala Ali

Created by and starring Youssef, this show follows Ramy Hassan, a first-generation Egyptian American living in New Jersey with his family who goes on a spiritual quest to explore facets of his community by volunteering at and spending time in a Sufi mosque. He’s caught up between both of his identities and strives to make sense of the world while believing life is just a morality test.
Stars: Devery Jacobs, Paulina Alexis, D’Pharaoh-Woon-A-Tai, Lane Factor, Zahn McClarnon, Sarah Podemski, Dallas Goldtooth, Gary Farmer, Elva Guerra

Sterlin Harjo and Taika Waititi’s sublime, heartwarming comedy tells the coming-of-age story of four Indigenous teens from rural Oklahoma who are mourning the death of their friend and trying to honor his wishes by going to California. The show’s fantastic third and final season wrapped up in 2023.

Stars: Alex Hassell, David Tennant, Aidan Turner, Bella Maclean, Emily Atak, Katherine Parkinson, Claire Rushbrook, Danny Dyer, Luke Pasqualino, Victoria Smurfit, Nafessa Williams, Oliver Chris, Hayley Atwell, Rupert Everett

Based on the bestselling novels by the late Dame Jilly Cooper, this salacious 1980s-set soap opera is full of corporate backstabbing, ill-advised affairs, sky-high shoulder pads, and cutting social commentary is the most unabashedly fun thing on television right now. The show centers on the ongoing feud between posh politician Rupert Campbell-Black (Hassell) and network executive Lord Tony Baddingham (Tennant) over the future of a local television franchise, but there’s plenty of drama to be had among all the Cotswolds’ residents. The second half of season 2 will air later this year, and the series has been renewed for a third season.
Cast: Lola Petticrew, Hazel Doupe, Anthony Boyle, Josh Finan, Maxine Peake, Frank Blake

Based on the book of the same name by journalist Patrick Radden O’Keefe, Say Nothing is a sprawling yet deeply personal account of the Troubles in Ireland, told across decades and lifetimes that see firebrand young IRA members grow into weary adults left to wonder whether all the violence was worth it. Lola Petticrew and Hazel Doupe are fantastic as two sisters drawn into the group, and though the show doesn’t offer any easy answers to the many questions it raises, it remains deeply compelling and empathetic to all its characters throughout.
Stars: Hiroyuki Sanada, Anna Sawai, Cosmo Jarvis, Tadanobu Asano, Takehiro Hira, Fumi Nikaido, Moeka Hoshi

Shōgun, FX’s adaptation of James Clavell’s sweeping Japan-set novel, weaves thrilling, action-packed drama with moving, character-driven stories. The 10-episode series also finally gives Hiroyuki Sanada the leading role he deserves, and it boasts breakout performances by Anna Sawai, Tadanobu Asani, and Moeka Hoshi. Expect stunning visuals, plenty of fight scenes, heartbreak, and jaw-dropping political chess games. The show has been renewed for two more seasons.
Stars: Damson Idris, Emily Rios, Carter Hudson, Sergio Peris-Mencheta, Amin Joseph, Michael Hyatt

Created by John Singleton, Eric Amadio, and Dave Andron, Snowfall is a gripping tale that kicks off in 1983 during the early days of L.A.’s crack epidemic. Idris plays Franklin, a street entrepreneur on a quest for power who is on a collision course with Lucia, the daughter of a Mexican crime lord. The series concluded with its sixth and final season in 2023, but a spin-off, The Drop: A Snowfall Saga, is set to premiere in September.
